# Unbounded type for semigroups generated by five consecutive squares

## Finding
For every integer \(k\ge4\), let \(n=12k\) and
\[
S_k=\langle n^2,(n+1)^2,(n+2)^2,(n+3)^2,(n+4)^2\rangle.
\]
Let \(\operatorname{PF}(S)\) be the set of pseudo-Frobenius numbers (integers \(f\notin S\) such that \(f+s\in S\) for every nonzero \(s\in S\)), and \(t(S)=|\operatorname{PF}(S)|\) its type. Then
\[
\boxed{t(S_k)\ge 2k.}
\]
More explicitly, put \(a=n^2\), \(g_i=(n+i)^2\) for \(1\le i\le4\), and define
\[
f_{k,j}=5g_2+2j g_3+(3k-1-j)g_4-a,
\qquad 0\le j\le2k-1.
\]
All \(2k\) of these numbers are distinct pseudo-Frobenius numbers of \(S_k\). In particular the type is unbounded in this fixed five-generator family of consecutive squares.

## Assumptions and scope
All semigroups are additive submonoids of the nonnegative integers. Since \(\gcd(n,n+1)=1\), the semigroups are numerical (cofinite). For \(n\ge48\), the five displayed generators are the unique minimal generators: they are distinct and each is smaller than \(2n^2\), so none can be a nonnegative sum of two or more of the other generators. Thus the embedding dimension is exactly five. The theorem is a lower bound for the stated congruence subfamily, not a formula for the exact type of every five-square semigroup.

## Proof
Fix integers \(k\ge4\) and \(0\le j\le2k-1\), write \(f=f_{k,j}\), and abbreviate \(a=n^2\) and \(g_i=(n+i)^2\). First verify the following four exact integer identities:
\[
\begin{aligned}
f+g_1&=2g_2+(5+2j)g_3+(3k-3-j)g_4,\\
f+g_2&=(8+2j)g_3+(3k-4-j)g_4,\\
f+g_3&=(3k-4-j)a+(9+2j)g_1+g_2,\\
f+g_4&=(3k-2-j)a+(4+2j)g_1+4g_2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Every coefficient on the right is nonnegative under the indicated hypotheses, hence \(f+g_i\in S_k\) for \(i=1,2,3,4\); also \(f+a=5g_2+2jg_3+(3k-1-j)g_4\in S_k\). Once \(f\notin S_k\) is proved, the displayed generator checks imply the defining pseudo-Frobenius condition for all nonzero semigroup elements.

We now prove \(f\notin S_k\), without any finite-experiment assumption. Put
\[
T_0=3k+3+j,\quad L_0=12k+6+2j,\quad Q_0=48k+4+2j.
\]
By expansion of the five-square expression,
\[
f=T_0 n^2+2nL_0+Q_0=(T_0+2)n^2+R,
\quad R=192k+48kj+4+2j.
\]
For \(k\ge4\) and \(0\le j\le2k-1\),
\[
0<R\le96k^2+148k+2<144k^2=n^2.
\]
Consequently any hypothetical representation \(f=\sum_{i=0}^4c_i(n+i)^2\), with \(c_i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\), has total coefficient \(T=\sum c_i\le T_0+2\), since each generator is at least \(n^2\).

Set \(L=\sum i c_i\), \(Q=\sum i^2c_i\) and \(\delta=T-T_0\). Comparing powers of \(n=12k\) gives
\[
\delta n^2+2n(L-L_0)+(Q-Q_0)=0.
\]
Thus \(Q-Q_0\) is divisible by \(n\); write \(Q=Q_0+24kv\) and \(L=L_0-6k\delta-v\) for some integer \(v\). (The coefficient of \(n\) is even because \(n\) is even.) Since \(Q\equiv L\pmod2\) and \(Q_0,L_0\) are even, \(v\) is even. Let \(s=v+2\delta\), also even.

For the deficit variables \(d_i=4-i\in\{0,1,2,3,4\}\), define
\[
U=\sum c_id_i=4T-L,
\qquad W=\sum c_id_i^2=Q-8L+16T.
\]
As \(d_i\le d_i^2\le4d_i\), every representation satisfies \(0\le U\le W\le4U\). Substitution yields the exact formulas
\[
U=6+2j+(6k+2)\delta+s,
\qquad W=4+2j+(24k+8)s.
\]
If \(s<0\), the evenness of \(s\) gives \(s\le-2\), forcing \(W<0\), impossible. If \(s=0\), then \(U\le W\) forces \(\delta\le-1\), which in turn forces
\[
U\le6+2(2k-1)-(6k+2)=2-2k<0.
\]
Thus \(s\ge2\). From \(W\le4U\),
\[
(24k+4)s\le20+6j+(24k+8)\delta.
\]
Since \(s\ge2\) and \(j\le2k-1\), the right-hand side with \(\delta\le1\) is at most \(36k+22\), whereas the left-hand side is at least \(48k+8>36k+22\) for \(k\ge4\). Therefore \(\delta\ge2\); the total-coefficient bound already gives \(\delta\le2\), so \(\delta=2\).

If \(s=2\), then \(v=s-2\delta=-2\), giving \(Q=4+2j\) and \(L=8+2j\), contrary to \(Q\ge L\) (since \(i^2\ge i\) for nonnegative integral \(i\)). If \(s\ge4\), then \(v=s-4\ge0\), whence \(Q\ge48k+4+2j\) while \(L=10+2j-s\le6+2j\). Consequently \(Q>4L\) for \(k\ge4\), \(j\le2k-1\), contrary to \(i^2\le4i\) for \(0\le i\le4\). Every possible even \(s\) has been excluded. Thus \(f\notin S_k\).

Finally, consecutive witnesses differ by
\[
f_{k,j+1}-f_{k,j}=2g_3-g_4=n^2+4n+2>0.
\]
They are therefore distinct pseudo-Frobenius numbers, proving \(t(S_k)\ge2k\) and unboundedness. \(\square\)

## Verification
The independent residue-class shortest-path implementation in `verify.py` computes the Apéry set modulo \(n^2\) and the full pseudo-Frobenius type. For \(k=4,5,6,7,8,9,10\), the exact computed types are respectively \(47,57,68,78,89,99,110\), all exceeding the proved lower bounds \(8,10,12,14,16,18,20\). It individually verifies the exhibited \(98\) pseudo-Frobenius witnesses, their generator sums, and the inequalities. Additional exact-integer formula checks cover \(k=11,20,50,100,1000\) without building Apéry tables. Run `python3 verify.py` with the Python standard library; no external packages are needed. The unrestricted argument above uses symbolic inequalities, not numerical extrapolation.

## Relationship to prior work
Kazimierz Chomicz, *On numerical semigroups with embedding dimension four* (arXiv:2604.25653, first public April 28, 2026), determines Apéry sets and invariants for **four** consecutive squares. Its Section 6 also discusses growth questions for finitely many consecutive-square generators. Those formulas do not determine the pseudo-Frobenius type of the distinct **five**-generator family here, and the manuscript does not state unbounded type for that family. Moscariello and Strazzanti, *Nearly Gorenstein numerical semigroups with five generators have bounded type* (arXiv:2501.08260), addresses the special nearly Gorenstein class; no nearly Gorenstein assumption is made here. The displayed explicit \(2k\)-element pseudo-Frobenius family is the asserted contribution, not the general concept that fixed-embedding-dimension semigroups can have unbounded type.

## Limitations
The bound is not claimed sharp, and no full type formula or Apéry classification is proved. The method establishes unboundedness along \(n\equiv0\pmod{12}\) with \(n\ge48\); other residue classes are not settled. Historical-priority assessment is based on targeted mathematical-record searches and inspected accessible primary material, not a guarantee against earlier equivalent results under other terminology. Independent mathematical review has not been performed.
